definition.definition: The reusable template describing the process flow — nodes, transitions, and variables.

version.definition: A specific snapshot of a definition. Lifecycle: Draft → Published → Retired.

draft.definition: An editable version that is not yet available for production bindings.

published.definition: A read-only version that can be bound to module screens and triggers.

binding.definition: A link between an organization, module screen, trigger event, and a published workflow version.

assignment_key.definition: A named role slot in the definition (for example REVIEWERS). Mapped to an org group at binding time.

assignment_group.definition: An organization-level group of participants who can receive tasks for a mapped assignment key.

outcome.definition: A decision result from a User Task (Approve, Reject, Return for Changes, and similar).

transition.definition: A directed connection between two activities, optionally keyed to an outcome or condition.

exclusive_gateway.definition: A decision point where exactly one outgoing path is taken.

inclusive_gateway.definition: Starts every outgoing path whose condition matches (OR-split).

call_activity.definition: Invokes another workflow definition as a sub-process, optionally waiting for completion.

parallel_gateway.definition: Splits execution into multiple simultaneous paths.

join_gateway.definition: Merges multiple paths back into one when all required branches complete.

sla_policy.definition: Reusable timing rules for deadlines, reminders, and escalations on User Tasks.

screen_key.definition: workflow identifier linking a company workflow binding to a module screen (for example workflow.start).

shadow_mode.definition: Binding mode where the workflow runs for observation without writing production module effects.

active_mode.definition: Full production mode. Tasks are assigned and outcomes apply to the module.

paused_mode.definition: Binding stays configured but temporarily stops starting new instances (for example during an incident).

disabled_mode.definition: Binding is saved for configuration only — no workflow starts from triggers.

simulate.definition: Dry-run a binding with sample JSON to preview steps, warnings, and errors without a live instance.

dead_letter.definition: An inbox or outbox integration message that failed permanently and can be replayed after fixing the root cause.

workload.definition: Dashboard of open, overdue, claimed, and completed-today work by assignment group.

set_variables.definition: A Script Task that safely assigns workflow variables via whitelist expressions — no arbitrary code.

wait_for_event.definition: Pauses the instance until an external correlated event arrives (event key + correlation variable).

work_item.definition: A task instance assigned to participants during workflow execution.

instance.definition: A running execution of a workflow version for a specific business entity and organization.

path-admin-go-live.title: Go live with a company workflow
path-admin-go-live.summary: Ordered workflow designers path from first definition to monitored production traffic.
path-admin-go-live.s1_body: Open Workflow → Definitions and create a new definition with a stable key (for example simple-approval) and bilingual name. NWFM creates Draft v1 automatically.
path-admin-go-live.s1_tip: Use a key that matches the business capability so bindings and APIs stay readable.
path-admin-go-live.s2_title: Open draft and draw the flow
path-admin-go-live.s2_body: Open the draft in the Designer. Place Start → User Task → End as the smallest useful flow. Connect nodes by dragging from ports or using quick-add.
path-admin-go-live.s2_tip: Save often. Only Draft versions are editable; published versions are read-only.
path-admin-go-live.s3_body: Select the User Task and set Assignment Key, Outcomes (Approve / Reject / Return), SLA, and optional form fields. Require claim when only one person should work the item.
path-admin-go-live.s3_tip: Keep assignment keys symbolic (REVIEWERS). Map them later to each organization group.
path-admin-go-live.s4_body: Run Validate, fix every error, then Publish. Publishing freezes the version so bindings can safely reference it.
path-admin-go-live.s4_tip: Clone a published version when you need another change cycle.
path-admin-go-live.s5_body: In Bindings, create Module → Screen Key → Trigger → published Version. Choose the organization and start in Shadow or Disabled while you finish mappings.
path-admin-go-live.s5_tip: Screen Key ties the workflow to the correct company screen in the workflow UI.
path-admin-go-live.s6_title: Map assignment keys to org groups
path-admin-go-live.s6_body: On the binding, map each assignment key to an active Assignment Group for that organization. Shadow/Active require complete mappings.
path-admin-go-live.s6_tip: If the org has not created groups yet, ask them to finish Organization Manual steps first.
path-admin-go-live.s7_body: Use the binding wizard Simulate step (or return to the binding) and POST realistic sample JSON. Review steps, warnings, and errors before go-live.
path-admin-go-live.s7_tip: Simulation never starts a live instance — safe to iterate quickly.
path-admin-go-live.s8_body: Switch the binding to Active to make it available on Start workflow. Standalone results are recorded in workflow history.
path-admin-go-live.s8_tip: Shadow runs the path without applying production module side-effects.
path-admin-go-live.s9_title: Monitor instances, dead letters, and workload
path-admin-go-live.s9_body: Watch Instances for Running / Failed states, replay Dead Letters after root-cause fixes, and use Workload to see overdue pressure by group.
path-admin-go-live.s9_tip: Prefer fixing mappings or payloads before mass-replaying dead letters.

path-org-prepare.title: Prepare teams and process tasks
path-org-prepare.summary: Ordered Organization path from team setup to day-to-day task handling and workload.
path-org-prepare.s1_body: Open Workflow → Participants and register each team member who may claim or complete workflow tasks.
path-org-prepare.s1_tip: Only registered participants can be added to assignment groups.
path-org-prepare.s2_body: Create groups (for example Request Reviewers), choose an assignment strategy, and add participants as members with claim rights as needed.
path-org-prepare.s2_tip: Use clear bilingual group names so workflow designers mapping is unambiguous.
path-org-prepare.s3_body: Create departments if you route work by department and attach a default assignment group when useful.
path-org-prepare.s4_body: Assignment keys live inside the published workflow definition. Your organization creates the groups; workflow designers maps keys → groups on the binding.
path-org-prepare.s4_tip: If tasks never appear, ask workflow designers to confirm the key mapping for your org.
path-org-prepare.s5_body: Group Inbox lists pending work for groups you belong to. My Tasks lists items you own (claimed or directly assigned).
path-org-prepare.s5_tip: Claim from Group Inbox when Requires Claim is enabled.
path-org-prepare.s6_body: Claim the task, review instructions and form fields, then complete with an outcome such as Approve, Reject, or Return for Changes. Add comments or attachments when required.
path-org-prepare.s6_tip: Choosing the correct outcome drives the next transition in the flow.
path-org-prepare.s7_body: If you claimed a task by mistake or cannot finish it, Release it back to the group. Use Delegation when your product flow supports handing work to another eligible participant.
path-org-prepare.s7_tip: Releasing keeps the item visible to other group members again.
path-org-prepare.s8_body: Open Workflow Requests to see instances for your organization and drill into timeline, current activity, and incidents.
path-org-prepare.s9_body: Check open, overdue, claimed, and completed-today metrics per assignment group to balance staffing.

overview.title: How NWFM Workflow fits together
overview.summary: Design-time templates, workflow bindings, and runtime task execution in one picture.
overview.s1_body: Definitions, drafts, Designer canvas, validation, and publish produce immutable versions ready for bindings.
overview.s2_body: Bindings attach a published version to Organization + Module + Screen + Trigger, then map assignment keys to org groups.
overview.s3_body: Use Start workflow to create a request. Tasks appear in the selected participant’s inbox. Completing outcomes advances the flow.
overview.s3_tip: Shadow mode lets workflow designers verify the path before Active production effects.
overview.s4_body: Monitor instances, workload, incidents, and dead letters. Clone published versions to iterate safely.

roles.title: Who does what
roles.summary: Feature areas in NWFM. These are guide categories, not access roles.
roles.s1_body: Create definitions, design versions, publish, bind to company screens, map keys, simulate, and control Disabled / Shadow / Active / Paused.
roles.s2_title: Set up participants and process tasks
roles.s2_body: Register participants, build assignment groups, claim and complete work, track requests, and watch workload.
roles.s3_body: Use the participant selector in the header to attribute task actions. NWFM currently has no login or access roles.

create-definition.title: Create a workflow definition
create-definition.summary: Create the reusable process template your versions and bindings will reference.
create-definition.s1_body: Go to Workflow → Definitions and choose New Definition.
create-definition.s2_body: Provide Definition Key, Name (EN), Name (AR), and optional description. Keys should be stable for integrations.
create-definition.s2_tip: Avoid renaming keys later — bindings and documentation rely on them.
create-definition.s3_body: Create the definition. Draft v1 is created automatically and listed under Versions.
create-definition.s4_body: From the definition row, open Versions to design, validate, publish, clone, or retire.
create-definition.s4_tip: Only one editable draft exists per definition at a time.

open-draft-draw.title: Open a draft and draw the flow
open-draft-draw.summary: Build the minimal Start → User Task → End path before adding complexity.
open-draft-draw.s1_body: From Versions, open Designer on the Draft. Published versions open read-only.
open-draft-draw.s2_body: Drag Start, User Task, and End onto the canvas. Give the User Task a clear bilingual name.
open-draft-draw.s2_tip: Every valid flow needs exactly one Start and at least one End.
open-draft-draw.s3_body: Connect Start → User Task → End using ports, click-connect, or quick-add.
open-draft-draw.s4_body: Save often. Your draft remains editable until you validate and publish.
open-draft-draw.s4_tip: If you need a blank canvas, create a new draft; use Clone to copy a published base.

configure-user-task.title: Configure a User Task
configure-user-task.summary: Assignment key, outcomes, SLA, and form fields that drive human work.
configure-user-task.s1_body: In Assignment, enter the Assignment Key and choose requires-claim / allow-self-claim as needed.
configure-user-task.s1_tip: Keys are symbolic — groups are mapped later per organization.
configure-user-task.s2_body: Add bilingual outcomes such as Approve, Reject, and Return. Draw an outgoing transition for each outcome key.
configure-user-task.s3_body: Bind an SLA policy or set a custom duration and optional escalation key.
configure-user-task.s4_body: Add structured form fields the assignee fills when completing the task.
configure-user-task.s5_body: Optional OnEnter / OnOutcome actions and variable mappings keep the instance state in sync with modules.
configure-user-task.s5_tip: Prefer Actions Catalog keys rather than inventing unregistered action names.

validate-publish.title: Validate and publish a version
validate-publish.summary: Make a draft immutable and safe for bindings.
validate-publish.s1_body: Click Validate and resolve errors (missing transitions, outcomes without edges, duplicate keys, and similar).
validate-publish.s2_body: Publish stays disabled until validation passes.
validate-publish.s2_tip: Click an error in the panel to jump to the offending node.
validate-publish.s3_body: Publish and confirm. The version becomes read-only and available for bindings.
validate-publish.s3_tip: Publishing is irreversible for that version — clone to edit further.
validate-publish.s4_body: Clone the published version when policy or process changes are required.

bindings-saas.title: Create a workflow binding
bindings-saas.summary: Module → Screen → Trigger → Version is the workflow designers production path.
bindings-saas.s1_body: Go to Workflow → Bindings and start New Binding for the target organization.
bindings-saas.s2_body: Choose Standalone, entity WorkflowRequest, and trigger RequestSubmitted. The start screen uses active bindings.
bindings-saas.s2_tip: Wrong trigger selection is the most common “nothing started” cause.
bindings-saas.s3_title: Set Screen Key and version policy
bindings-saas.s3_body: Enter Screen Key (for example workflow.start) and choose latest published or a fixed version.
bindings-saas.s4_body: Optionally set input and outcome mappings so module payloads and workflow results stay aligned.
bindings-saas.s5_body: Review the summary, create the binding, then continue with key mapping and simulation.
bindings-saas.s5_tip: Keep the initial mode Shadow until the first end-to-end check passes.

group-mappings.title: Map assignment keys to groups
group-mappings.summary: Resolve symbolic keys to organization assignment groups on each binding.
group-mappings.s1_body: On the binding detail or wizard Map Keys step, list every assignment key from the published version.
group-mappings.s1_tip: Shadow and Active require complete mappings.
group-mappings.s2_body: For each key, select an active Assignment Group that owns that work in the company.
group-mappings.s3_body: Save mappings, then simulate or run Shadow. New instances use the saved routing; in-flight instances keep their original route.
group-mappings.s3_tip: Ask the organization to create missing groups before you activate.

simulate-binding.title: Simulate a binding
simulate-binding.summary: Dry-run routing and conditions with sample JSON before going live.
simulate-binding.s1_body: Build JSON that mirrors the real module trigger payload, including identifiers your conditions reference.
simulate-binding.s1_tip: Simulation needs a saved binding id — create the binding first.
simulate-binding.s2_body: Use the Simulate step to inspect evaluated steps, warnings, and errors.
simulate-binding.s3_body: Adjust conditions, mappings, or the definition draft, then simulate again until clean.
simulate-binding.s3_tip: Simulation does not create a live instance or tasks.

modes-shadow-active.title: Shadow verification then Active
modes-shadow-active.summary: Safe go-live pattern for company workflows.
modes-shadow-active.s1_body: Set binding mode to Shadow so instances and tasks can be observed without production module side-effects.
modes-shadow-active.s2_body: The Start workflow screen lists Active bindings. Use simulation to inspect routing before starting a live request; Shadow mode remains available for future event integrations.
modes-shadow-active.s2_tip: Check Monitor for failures or early termination.
modes-shadow-active.s3_body: Switch the binding to Active to make it available on Start workflow. Standalone results are recorded in workflow history.
modes-shadow-active.s4_body: Paused keeps configuration but stops new starts — useful during incidents or migrations.
modes-shadow-active.s4_tip: Disabled is for configuration-only periods before any runtime.

monitor-ops.title: Monitor instances and operations
monitor-ops.summary: workflow designers operational loop for reliability.
monitor-ops.s1_body: Open Instances to filter by organization/status and inspect timelines for Running, Failed, or Suspended work.
monitor-ops.s2_body: Review Inbox/Outbox dead letters and replay only after fixing root causes.
monitor-ops.s3_body: Use Workload to spot overdue and claimed tasks for the active tenant.
monitor-ops.s4_body: Track workflow incidents and keep business calendars / SLA policies accurate for due dates.
monitor-ops.s4_tip: Couple monitor checks with the Troubleshooting guide when patterns repeat.

register-participants.title: Register workflow participants
register-participants.summary: Make team members eligible for assignment groups and tasks.
register-participants.s1_body: Go to Workflow → Participants and choose Register Participant.
register-participants.s2_body: Enter a name, email, optional Arabic name and employee number, then register. No user account is required.
register-participants.s2_tip: The header list updates automatically. The configured default participant must remain active.
register-participants.s3_body: Confirm the participant appears as active before adding them to groups.

assignment-groups.title: Create assignment groups
assignment-groups.summary: Group participants and choose how new tasks are offered.
assignment-groups.s1_body: Open Assignment Groups, create a group with code and bilingual names, and pick a strategy (Manual, Round Robin, and others).
assignment-groups.s2_body: Add registered participants, set claim rights, and primary flags if used by your process.
assignment-groups.s3_title: Share the group name with workflow designers
assignment-groups.s3_body: workflow designers maps workflow assignment keys to this group on the binding.
assignment-groups.s3_tip: Keep codes stable; they appear in operational reports.

departments.title: Optional departments
departments.summary: Organize participants by department when routing needs it.
departments.s1_body: Open Departments and create bilingual name/code. Optionally attach a default assignment group.
departments.s2_body: Attach participants who should be associated with that department.

assignment-keys-note.title: Assignment keys — what orgs need to know
assignment-keys-note.summary: Keys are designed by workflow designers; organizations supply the groups.
assignment-keys-note.s1_title: Keys are not created in the org panel
assignment-keys-note.s1_body: Assignment keys are embedded in the published workflow. Your job is to provide named groups with the right people.
assignment-keys-note.s1_tip: Ask workflow designers which keys exist for each binding your company uses.
assignment-keys-note.s2_body: If Group Inbox stays empty after a known trigger, confirm your groups are active and ask workflow designers to verify key mappings and binding mode.

my-tasks-inbox.title: My Tasks vs Group Inbox
my-tasks-inbox.summary: Where work appears and when to claim it.
my-tasks-inbox.s1_body: Shows work already assigned or claimed by you.
my-tasks-inbox.s2_body: Shows pending items for assignment groups you belong to.
my-tasks-inbox.s3_body: If Requires Claim is enabled, claim before you can complete. Claimed items move into My Tasks.
my-tasks-inbox.s3_tip: Do not claim work you cannot finish the same day unless your policy allows it.

claim-complete.title: Claim and complete tasks
claim-complete.summary: Move a work item from pending to a recorded outcome.
claim-complete.s1_body: From Group Inbox or My Tasks, open the task detail and read instructions.
claim-complete.s2_body: Claim ownership so other group members cannot complete the same item.
claim-complete.s2_tip: Release promptly if you cannot proceed.
claim-complete.s3_body: Choose Approve, Reject, Return, or another configured outcome. Fill required comments, attachments, and form fields.
claim-complete.s4_body: After Complete, the workflow advances. Track residual progress under Requests if needed.
claim-complete.s4_tip: Wrong outcome selection can send the case down an unintended path — read labels carefully (EN/AR).

delegate-release.title: Delegate and release
delegate-release.summary: Recover gracefully when ownership needs to change.
delegate-release.s1_body: Use Release when you claimed a task but another group member should take it.
delegate-release.s1_tip: After release, the item returns to pending in Group Inbox.
delegate-release.s2_body: Where delegation is enabled, hand the task to another eligible participant instead of completing it yourself.
delegate-release.s3_body: Stale claims inflate overdue counts. Release or complete promptly.

track-requests.title: Track request progress
track-requests.summary: Follow organization instances from start to finish.
track-requests.s1_body: List instances started for your organization and open one for detail.
track-requests.s2_body: Inspect current activity, activity history, and event timeline.
track-requests.s3_body: If an incident is listed, coordinate with workflow designers or your Reviewer process owners.
track-requests.s3_tip: Progress views are read-oriented — task actions still happen in My Tasks / Inbox.

workload.title: Workload dashboard
workload.summary: See open, overdue, and claimed pressure by assignment group.
workload.s1_body: Open Workload to inspect assignment groups in the active tenant.
workload.s2_body: Review open, overdue, and completed-today totals, then scan pending/overdue/claimed by group.
workload.s3_body: Add members, rebalance groups, or ask workflow designers to adjust SLA / routing when overdue stays high.
workload.s3_tip: Combine Workload with Group Inbox clearing rituals.

draw-connect.title: Draw and connect nodes
draw-connect.summary: Three reliable ways to wire the Designer canvas.
draw-connect.s1_body: Hover a node to reveal ports, drag from an outgoing port, and drop on a valid target.
draw-connect.s1_tip: The cursor becomes a crosshair over a valid port.
draw-connect.s2_body: Click a source port, then click a highlighted target. Press Escape to cancel.
draw-connect.s3_body: Select a node, use the + control, pick the next node type, and let Designer create and connect it.
draw-connect.s3_tip: Label outcome-driven edges with the matching outcome key.

node-reference.title: Node reference
node-reference.summary: What each major node type is for.
node-reference.s1_body: Exactly one Start begins the flow. One or more End nodes terminate it. Start has no incoming edges; End has no outgoing edges.
node-reference.s2_body: User Tasks assign human work. Service Tasks run registered catalog actions automatically.
node-reference.s3_body: Set Variables safely assigns whitelist expressions. Notification sends a configured channel message.
node-reference.s4_body: Timer pauses for a duration/date. Wait for Event resumes when a correlated external event arrives.
node-reference.s5_body: Exclusive chooses one path; Inclusive starts matching paths; Parallel forks; Join merges branches.
node-reference.s6_body: Starts another definition by key as a sub-process, optionally waiting for completion.
node-reference.s6_tip: Validate after major node changes — gateway edge counts are a common failure.

outcomes.title: Configure outcomes
outcomes.summary: Decisions that drive User Task transitions.
outcomes.s1_body: For each decision, set Key, Label EN, Label AR, and flags (default, requires comment/attachment).
outcomes.s2_body: Draw an outgoing edge for each outcome and label/key it to match.
outcomes.s2_tip: Validation fails if an outcome has no matching transition.
outcomes.s3_body: Keep outcome keys stable so binding outcome mapping can write results back to the module.

actions.title: Task actions
actions.summary: Automated steps on enter, complete, outcome, or failure.
actions.s1_body: Choose OnEnter, OnComplete, OnOutcome, or OnFailure and reference an Actions Catalog key.
actions.s2_body: Continue, Retry, FailActivity, FailWorkflow, or CreateIncident depending on risk.
actions.s3_body: Verify action behaviour in Shadow with realistic payloads.
actions.s3_tip: FailWorkflow terminates the whole instance — use sparingly.

variables.title: Workflow variables
variables.summary: Typed instance data shared across nodes.
variables.s1_body: Open the Variables drawer and add Key, Name, Type, and optional default.
variables.s2_body: Use input/output mappings on tasks and binding input mapping for module payloads.
variables.s2_tip: Mark sensitive variables so UI/audit masking stays correct.
variables.s3_body: Assign whitelist expressions without arbitrary script execution.

sla.title: SLA on User Tasks
sla.s1_body: Manage policies under Workflow → SLA Policies and attach calendars when using business hours.
sla.s2_body: On the User Task SLA tab, select a policy or enter a custom duration and escalation key.
sla.s3_body: SLA edits on a draft only apply after validate/publish and binding to that version.
sla.s3_tip: Overdue KPIs in Workload depend on correct due dates from SLA.

dead-letters.title: Dead letters
dead-letters.s1_body: Inspect Inbox Dead Letters and Failed Outbox columns (id, module, entity, error, created).
dead-letters.s2_body: Correct payload shape, binding mode/mappings, or downstream errors before replay.
dead-letters.s2_tip: Mass replay without a fix usually recreates the same failures.
dead-letters.s3_body: Replay individual messages and confirm Monitor / module state recovers.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting common issues
troubleshooting.summary: Fast checks for design-time and runtime failures.
troubleshooting.s1_body: Ensure Start/End rules, transitions, outcome edges, and unique keys are satisfied. Publish requires Valid status.
troubleshooting.s2_body: Only drafts are editable. Clone a published version to create a new draft.
troubleshooting.s3_body: Check binding mode (not Disabled/Paused), complete key mappings, active groups/members, and that Monitor shows a started instance.
troubleshooting.s4_body: Open instance detail, read the failed step and failure reason. Review action failure policies and required variables.
troubleshooting.s5_title: Mapping changed but old routing remains
troubleshooting.s5_body: Mappings apply to new instances. In-flight work keeps the routing captured at start.
troubleshooting.s5_tip: Cancel erroneous instances only with a clear operational reason.
troubleshooting.s6_body: Drag from the port handle, not the node body. Drop on the target node. Use Escape to leave connect mode.

modes-reference.title: Binding mode meanings
modes-reference.summary: Disabled, Shadow, Active, and Paused at a glance.
modes-reference.s1_body: Binding is stored for configuration. Triggers do not start workflows.
modes-reference.s2_body: Workflow runs for observation/audit without applying production module effects.
modes-reference.s3_body: Production mode. Tasks assign and outcomes apply. Requires complete assignment key mappings.
modes-reference.s4_body: Configuration retained; new instance starts are temporarily stopped (incidents, freezes).

standalone-walkthrough.title: Run the sample approval
standalone-walkthrough.summary: Start, claim, and complete the seeded workflow in NWFM.
standalone-walkthrough.s1_body: The header shows tenant NWFM and the selected participant. Reviewer 1 and Reviewer 2 belong to the Reviewers group.
standalone-walkthrough.s1_tip: Selecting a participant changes action attribution without a login.
standalone-walkthrough.s2_body: Open Designer & definitions, then the Simple approval version. The published flow is Start → Review request → Completed.
standalone-walkthrough.s2_tip: Clone the version to make changes.
standalone-walkthrough.s3_body: The review task is assigned to the Reviewers group.
standalone-walkthrough.s3_tip: Add participants to groups before assigning them work.
standalone-walkthrough.s4_body: Open Start workflow, select the standalone binding, enter a request reference, and start.
standalone-walkthrough.s4_tip: Use a meaningful reference to find the request later.
standalone-walkthrough.s5_body: The binding uses Standalone / WorkflowRequest / RequestSubmitted and screen key workflow.start.
standalone-walkthrough.s5_tip: Active mode makes the binding available on the start screen.
standalone-walkthrough.s6_body: Open Tasks and claim the available review task as Reviewer 1 or Reviewer 2.
standalone-walkthrough.s6_tip: Only the participant who owns the task can complete it.
standalone-walkthrough.s7_body: Open Action, enter Approve, add a comment if useful, and complete.
standalone-walkthrough.s7_tip: Custom workflows can define named outcomes and required form fields.
standalone-walkthrough.s8_body: Open Requests or Execution monitor. The sample request is Completed and its history records the action.
standalone-walkthrough.s8_tip: Existing instances retain their published workflow version.
standalone-walkthrough.s9_body: Create definitions, configure assignments, validate, publish, and bind them to the standalone start screen.
standalone-walkthrough.s9_tip: No external business module is required.
